body:
## Why

Foundryline now has demonstrated **Discover** and **Maintain** patterns, including a read-only GitHub Actions maintenance run. Our third pattern, **Deliver**, should explain how an **explicitly approved task** becomes an implementation candidate, is checked with the existing Proofline CLI, and reaches a **reviewable PR** only after a separate publication decision.

Deliver must be a **copyable manual blueprint**, not a new coding controller or mandatory Intentline/Proofline chain. Implement [Foundryline Milestone E](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/blob/main/IMPLEMENTATION.md) using current verified peer interfaces, with honest runtime/host limits.

## Current upstream pins and supported scope (as of issue creation)

- [Intentline `25e926f57e69395193fc0ac258f9e6dd2332cb18`](https://github.com/grove/intentline/tree/25e926f57e69395193fc0ac258f9e6dd2332cb18): optional offline acceptance draft; `export --format json` supports one initial schema-1 revision-1 S1 acceptance record.
- [Proofline `8e117fff4de2459637fe7f74f47ab17fc3341d84`](https://github.com/grove/proofline/tree/8e117fff4de2459637fe7f74f47ab17fc3341d84): `proofline.py check --repo --source --command/--checks` works **without Intentline**, and optionally `--intentline-export DIR` plus `--intentline-links FILE`; imported R IDs without explicit links start **NOT DEMONSTRATED**. `check` needs **macOS, Python 3.11+, exact Codex CLI 0.162.1** native sandbox and a Git repo. Offline Linux tests **do not** qualify native Proofline runs. No unsafe fallback is allowed.
- The optional adapter **rejects** amended/child/multi-source/revised/partial/changed exports. Never flatten history or discard original requirements to make an export importable.
- Proofline is **check evidence, not authority, proof of completeness or issue/PR publishing permission**. Explicitly authorize agent edits, selected check execution, PR publication and merging **separately**.

## Requested deliverables

- `patterns/deliver.md`: short, copyable end-to-end manual route with inputs, output and refusal conditions for admission → optional Intentline draft → authorized coding agent edits → candidate freeze → selected Proofline native checks → review of outcomes/gaps → separately authorized PR/merge. Include direct check-only path without Intentline.
- `examples/manual-deliver/`: one **source-grounded and runnable** small implementation candidate/example, an exact original request and check commands (or argument arrays), explicit requirement-to-check mapping where applicable, provenance, and one check that deliberately remains **NOT DEMONSTRATED** without a linked command. Distinguish a synthetic teaching fixture from an **actually observed** native Proofline check. Use real upstream compatibility fixtures/receipts **as external evidence with pinned source links**, not falsely claimed Foundryline runs.
- A clear **negative/refusal** matrix for unsupported Intentline exports, missing native sandbox, stale/frozen candidate, absent executable, missing permission and truncated evidence. No partial evidence may become a passing/approved delivery.
- Python reference checks and, if useful, runnable fixture unit tests in `checks/` or the example that validate links, file identities, authored source citations, named gates, and no invented runtime/approval claims. These offline checks do **not** substitute for a native Proofline run.
- Update README and IMPLEMENTATION to link the new recipe with a precise **reference provided / live qualification pending** status.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **R1 — Manual copyable route.** The Deliver guide names actual pinned tools, compatible host/CLI versions, exact supported commands, and effect gates; a coding agent is chosen and authorized by the adopting project, not launched implicitly.
- [ ] **R2 — Optional planning.** The direct Proofline check path works without Intentline; the optional Intentline S1/revision-1 JSON export path is faithful to upstream CLI flags/identity rules, and does not silently treat saved acceptance or approval metadata as authority.
- [ ] **R3 — Worked source/candidate example.** A small, reviewable example shows an original request, implemented candidate, bounded selected test(s), command identity, a separate untouched requirement and what was not assessed. Mark authored examples vs actual execution unambiguously.
- [ ] **R4 — Real native evidence.** On a **qualified macOS/Codex CLI 0.162.1 host**, run Proofline's actual check-only path with a frozen candidate and selected commands; retain CLI version, source/candidate/tree identities, exact argv, native sandbox, receipt hashes, result/status and costs/time where observable. A mock, fixture or Linux structural CI is **not** live native evidence.
- [ ] **R5 — Refusal/negative controls.** Retain real observed refusal/absence for at least one missing sandbox/command/unsupported export/stale candidate case when safely possible; authored descriptions are clearly **PROPOSED — NOT RUN**. Never hide blocked/unknown states.
- [ ] **R6 — Bounded assessment.** Reports distinguish `CHECKS PASSED` (only selected check evidence), `CHECKS FAILED`, `CHECKS UNAVAILABLE`, `EXECUTION UNAVAILABLE`, `STALE CHECKS`, `NOT DEMONSTRATED` and `coverage_completeness: UNKNOWN`. No overall acceptance certification.
- [ ] **R7 — Independent handoff / approvals.** Retain a reviewable example handoff/PR proposal and separate decision points for coding, checks, PR CREATE, merge, deployment. No automatic PR or unapproved GitHub writes.
- [ ] **R8 — Reviewable PR and validation.** Python reference/unit tests pass, documentation links resolve; native/live claims remain explicitly pending until independently observed. PR stays unmerged pending maintainer review.

## Proposed verification — NOT RUN by this issue

1. Confirm actual upstream pins/flags and sample export shape, including proofline native host requirements.
2. Implement the minimal manual guide and source/test teaching example; run regular Python tests as ordinary tests (not as Proofline native receipts).
3. On a **qualified host only**, exercise an actual Proofline `check` and negative case; retain and independently inspect machine-readable output. If host isn't available, **do not claim R4/R5 complete** and keep live qualification open.
4. Review the original requirement vs all R IDs and chosen check behavior, looking for a deliberately unlinked obligation; record all limitations.
5. Open a reviewable PR; do not merge, issue publish or deploy without explicit separate grants.

## Non-goals

A hosted factory, new mandatory controller, LLM verifier, general Intentline-to-P2P schema bridge, Linux-native Proofline checks, automatic issue/PR publication, complete requirements attestation, or conversion of P2P contracts.

**Definition of done:** A useful, honest Deliver recipe with one genuinely witnessed native candidate-and-check run, a negative/refusal observation, an independent review of evidence/limits and a **separately authorized** PR decision. A document-only PR is valuable progress but **not** the native qualification described in R4.

## Implementation status — 2026-10-18

[PR #19](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/pull/19) is **open, not merged**. It adds a copyable manual Deliver pattern, an authored two-line username example with source-cited R1/R2 obligations, tests, optional (not exercised) initial S1 Intentline export commands, an unpublished handoff, refusal cases, and bounded verification metadata.

**Observed native Proofline evidence (partial R4/R5):**
- **[macOS check-only run 39114778567](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/actions/runs/39114778567):** actual Ubuntu-independent macOS 15.7.9 ARM64 runner, Python 3.12, exact Codex CLI 0.162.1 and pinned Proofline `8e117fff4de2459637fe7f74f47ab17fc3341d84`. A frozen **authored** Git candidate was selected, native boundary canaries reported OBSERVED, one explicitly selected R1 test ran and produced **CHECKS PASSED** (CLI exit 0). No coding model invoked. Original source hash, frozen candidate tree and real selected argv retained.
- **Witnessed negative:** Same native checker with an intentionally absent selected command produced **CHECKS UNAVAILABLE** (CLI exit 2, no product assertion), not a false failing product test.
- **Retained source:** [GitHub Actions artifact 12131743490](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/actions/runs/39114778567/artifacts/12131743490), ZIP digest `e4e9722c02f0bdfd35639e8045cf7f1a24bbf102055dc572d1628e9e9f358797`, expires **2026-10-25**. The actual ZIP was downloaded and inspected. [Written receipt summary](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/blob/feat/manual-deliver-reference/examples/manual-deliver/native-qualification.md) and [structured readback](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/blob/feat/manual-deliver-reference/examples/manual-deliver/native-qualification.json) are committed for review.
- **Blocked first launch:** [run 39114638979](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/actions/runs/39114638979) hit a node-wrapper launcher gap inside the native sandbox; it was not a demonstrated code failure. The later successful attempt used the installed exact-version native Codex binary, without widening permissions.
- **Ordinary reference CI:** [Final run 39115339901](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/actions/runs/39115339901) passed **26/26 Python tests**, including authored fixture tests; not equivalent to native evidence.
- One-time macOS qualification workflow has been **removed from the PR's final file list**, avoiding ongoing model/runner expense.

**Remainder intentionally NOT DONE:** A coding-agent implementation of a **real approved issue**, a real Intentline JSON export and exact `R`-to-command import (optional path), independent complete original-behavior acceptance review, unlinked R2 proof, and permission for an actual delivery PR/merge. A green selected check provides limited evidence, **coverage completeness remains UNKNOWN**.

**Disposition:** PR #19 is a useful reference and genuinely demonstrates the native *check-only* portion, but **issue #18 remains OPEN** until a real approved coding-agent-to-candidate-to-PR handoff is separately authorized, executed, evidenced and reviewed. No automatic approval, publication, deployment or unsupported Linux native execution has been claimed.
